steps.title: Write its job
steps.subtitle: Tell your assistant exactly what it does
steps.teaches: A clear role, tone and format is what separates a real assistant from a search box.

turns.coach: Let's write your assistant's job description. When it writes for {audience}, should it lead with the headline number, or the story first?

sets.lead: Start with the headline number or result, then the supporting detail.
Start with a one-line summary of what happened, then the numbers behind it.
Start with the headline number or result, then the supporting detail.

turns.coach: Good. And the tone, short and punchy or more detail?

sets.tone: Direct and concise. Short sentences. No filler.
Thorough and explanatory, but never padded.
Concise by default, with detail where it matters.

turns.coach: Last one. Anything it should never do?

sets.constraint: Never invent or estimate numbers. If a figure is missing, ask for it.
Avoid jargon and buzzwords. Write so anyone can follow it.
Stick to what the data says. Do not add opinions or recommendations unless asked.

steps.closing: That is a real set of instructions. You just wrote the brain of your assistant.

steps.title: Give it your context
steps.subtitle: One real example teaches it your voice
steps.teaches: One real example of your own work does more than a page of description.

turns.coach: Now the part that makes it sound like you, not a generic AI. Do you have an old {task} you wrote? Even a few lines works.

steps.outputTemplate:
Example of my past work (match this style and structure):
"""
{example}
"""
steps.noExampleNote: No problem. Your Gem can also hold up to 10 knowledge files, so once you have a couple of {task} saved you can upload them later. We'll start without an example and refine after your first real use.
steps.closing: Your assistant now knows how you write, not just what to write.

steps.title: Build it for real
steps.subtitle: Create the actual Gem in Gemini
steps.teaches: This is the real thing: a saved assistant you can open any time, not a one-off chat.

turns.coach: Time to bring it to life. Open Gemini, then Gems, then New Gem. Paste in the name and the instructions you just built, and save.

help.stuck: Two things trip most people up. One: Gems live behind the menu on the left at gemini.google.com, not in the chat box. Two: the Instructions field is the big one, that is where your text goes. Your instructions are still saved here, so nothing is lost.

steps.closing: Your assistant exists now. It is saved in your Gemini account, and it is yours.

steps.title: Test it
steps.subtitle: Run it once and see what it does
steps.teaches: Testing before you rely on it is how you learn to steer an AI instead of hoping.

turns.coach: Let's test it. In Gemini, open your assistant and try this: "Draft a {task} for {audience}. Here's what happened this week: ..." then describe it in your own words.

branches.good: That is your assistant doing your work. Keep the instructions as they are for now.
branches.close: Normal, and easy to fix. Open the Gem, edit the Instructions, and add one line about what you wanted differently. Small edits beat rewrites.
branches.bad: Almost always one of two things: the instructions were too general, or it had no example to copy. Add a real example to the Instructions and try once more.

steps.closing: You just debugged an AI. That is the skill most people never pick up.

steps.title: Use it for real
steps.subtitle: Put it on an actual task, today
steps.teaches: An assistant you use is a skill. An assistant you built and never opened is a demo.

turns.coach: This is the moment it stops being an exercise. Do you have a real {task} due soon?
Go run it on that real task. Come back and tell me how it went.

steps.closing: You built an AI assistant and used it on real work. That is rung one, done.

completion.title: You built your first AI.
completion.body: Most people never get past using AI as a search box. You have a working assistant you made yourself.

nextRung.title: Give it your knowledge
nextRung.teaser: Feed it your documents so it knows your world, not just your style.
